annotations.keyFindings: In 9 trials, phlebitis and bloodstream infection did not differ between strategies and clinically indicated replacement led to fewer insertions; catheter failure was higher after a policy change in 3 of 11 cohort studies.
annotations.limitations: Search ended in June 2020; few studies accounted for several catheters per patient; most cohort studies did not adjust for changes in patient mix.

annotations.keyFindings: Across about 214,000 catheters in six hospitals the bloodstream infection rate was 0.08 per 1,000 catheter-days and was similar up to and beyond 96 hours; catheters inserted in the emergency department had about twice the rate.
annotations.limitations: Only 58 infections, so estimates by dwell time were imprecise; the hospitals used different replacement policies.

annotations.keyFindings: Ignoring several catheters per patient gave a hazard ratio of 1.24 (1.08 to 1.42) for dwell beyond 96 hours; a shared frailty model gave 1.12 (0.93 to 1.35).
annotations.limitations: One dataset; a methods case study rather than an evaluation of a policy.

annotations.keyFindings: The flowsheet removal reason was missing for 11 percent of 540 removals and agreed with bedside observation for 86 percent where recorded; removals on night shifts more often lacked a reason.
annotations.limitations: Four wards of one hospital; bedside observation by a single research nurse.

annotations.keyFindings: Insertion time fell from 41 to 26 minutes per 10 patients per day, while site assessment and documentation rose from 12 to 19 minutes.
annotations.limitations: Two wards and four weeks per period; observers knew the period; no complication data.

claims.text: After four surgical wards moved from routine to clinically indicated replacement, catheter failure occurred in 31 percent of catheters before and 33 percent after, in an unadjusted before-after comparison.
claims.passage: occurred in 31 percent of catheters before and 33 percent after
claims.interpretation: A planning value for the local comparison; unadjusted, so the small difference may reflect patient mix.

claims.text: On medical wards using clinically indicated replacement, phlebitis did not rise with dwell beyond 96 hours (4.1 per 1,000 catheter-days up to 96 hours and 3.8 afterwards), while site assessment was documented in 83 percent of shifts.
claims.passage: 4.1 per 1,000 catheter-days up to 96 hours and 3.8 per 1,000 catheter-days afterwards
claims.interpretation: Longer dwell need not mean more phlebitis where sites are scored every shift; documentation gaps are the weak point.

claims.text: In an interrupted time series over 18 months on each side of a switch to clinically indicated replacement, monthly catheter failure showed no step change (0.9 percentage points, 95 percent confidence interval -2.1 to 3.9) and no change in slope.
claims.passage: there was no step change at the switch (0.9 percentage points, 95 percent confidence interval -2.1 to 3.9) and no change in slope
claims.interpretation: A monthly series can separate a policy from trends; the same series showed a co-intervention (a catheter brand change).

claims.text: In 6,120 catheters from 2,874 admissions, ignoring several catheters per patient gave a hazard ratio of 1.24 for dwell beyond 96 hours, while a shared frailty model gave 1.12 with an interval of 0.93 to 1.35.
claims.passage: while a shared frailty model gave 1.12, with an interval of 0.93 to 1.35
claims.interpretation: The local analysis must account for several catheters per patient, or it may overstate a dwell effect.

claims.text: In a six-hospital surveillance cohort, peripheral catheter-associated bloodstream infection occurred at 0.08 per 1,000 catheter-days, with similar rates up to and beyond 96 hours but only 58 infections in total.
claims.passage: The infection rate was 0.08 per 1,000 catheter-days overall.
claims.interpretation: Bloodstream infection is too rare for a local comparison and should be reported as counts.

claims.text: Against bedside observation of 540 removals, the flowsheet removal reason was missing for 11 percent and, where recorded, agreed with the observed reason for 86 percent.
claims.passage: A removal reason was missing for 11 percent of removals.
claims.interpretation: Flowsheet removal reasons can measure failure if coded with a fixed rule and checked; local completeness must be measured at extraction.

synthesis: Ten retrieved records from two searches, appraised at abstract level. After moves to clinically indicated replacement, catheter failure was similar in a before-after cohort (31 and 33 percent) and in an interrupted time series, but higher after a policy change in 3 of 11 cohort studies in a systematic review whose 9 trials found no difference in phlebitis or bloodstream infection and fewer insertions. Phlebitis did not rise with dwell beyond 96 hours where sites were scored every shift, while infiltration rose after the fourth day in patients aged 75 and over. Ignoring several catheters per patient inflated a dwell effect from 1.12 to 1.24. Bloodstream infection is rare (0.08 per 1,000 catheter-days); flowsheet removal reasons were missing for 11 percent of removals in one validation; nursing time moved from insertion to site assessment.
gradeRationale: Overall certainty is not rated across these records: they address different outcomes with different designs, and one label would hide that. Per outcome: catheter failure after a policy change, low (observational comparisons with inconsistent results); phlebitis, low; infiltration in older patients, low; bloodstream infection, very low (few events, imprecise); insertions per patient, moderate (consistent in trials).
summary: Ten retrieved records appraised; six source-derived claims; no single overall certainty, with certainty stated per outcome in the rationale.
